questions.q:
Consider the following statements about shifting (jhum) cultivation:
1. It is practised only in North-East India.
2. It involves clearing vegetation, burning it and cultivating the patch for a few seasons.
3. Cultivators move to a new patch when fertility of the old patch declines.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Slash-and-burn farming rotates across patches as nutrients in the ash get used up. Shorter fallow periods caused by population pressure have made it a driver of forest and soil loss. It is not confined to the North-East, since Podu and Bewar are practised elsewhere.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Shifting cultivation name) with List-II (region):
List-I
A. Podu
B. Bewar
C. Kumari
D. Jhum
List-II
1. North-Eastern India
2. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
3. Western Ghats
4. Madhya Pradesh
questions.e: Podu is practised in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, Bewar in Madhya Pradesh, Kumari in the Western Ghats and Jhum in the North-East.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UNCCD:
1. It was adopted in 1994 and entered into force in 1996.
2. Its secretariat is located in Nairobi.
3. It focuses on arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Convention to Combat Desertification followed a call at the Rio Summit and is focused on drylands. Its permanent secretariat is in Bonn, Germany, whereas Nairobi hosts UNEP.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India hosted the 14th Conference of the Parties to the UNCCD in 2019.
2. India has pledged to restore 26 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.
3. India's earlier pledge under the Bonn Challenge was 21 million hectares by 2020.
4. The Bonn Challenge aims to restore 350 million hectares of degraded land by 2050.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The global Bonn Challenge target is 150 million hectares by 2020 and 350 million hectares by 2030, so statement 4 has the wrong year. India raised its own pledge from 21 to 26 million hectares at UNCCD COP14.

questions.q: The shrinking of the Aral Sea in Central Asia is mainly attributed to
o: melting of glaciers feeding the sea
diversion of water from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers for irrigation
questions.e: Large cotton irrigation schemes drew the two feeder rivers dry, so inflow fell below evaporation. The exposed salt-laden bed then turned into a new desert, the Aralkum.

questions.q: The Great Green Wall initiative of the African Union is aimed at
o: building a defensive barrier along the Sahara coast
creating an artificial forest along the Nile
restoring degraded landscapes across the Sahel to check desertification
questions.e: The initiative spans the Sahel, south of the Sahara, from Senegal to Djibouti. Trees, grasses and soil restoration are meant to stop the desert advancing.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Excessive canal irrigation in arid regions without proper drainage can make agricultural land saline.
Statement-II: Evaporation of water from the surface brings dissolved salts to the top soil, where they accumulate.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: In dry climates evaporation exceeds rainfall, so water drawn up by capillary action leaves salts behind. Waterlogging from over-irrigation raises the water table and speeds this up, as seen in parts of Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Which of the following terms is used in North India for saline and alkaline efflorescence on soil?
questions.e: Reh, Kallar and Usar are local names of salt-affected soils in the Indo-Gangetic plain. Khadar is new alluvium, Bhabar is the pebbly foothill belt, and Regur is black cotton soil.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about soil erosion:
1. Gully erosion leads to the formation of ravines such as those in the Chambal region.
2. Sheet erosion removes a thin uniform layer of top soil and often goes unnoticed.
3. Sheet erosion is more visible than gully erosion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sheet erosion is deceptive because the loss is gradual and spread evenly, whereas gullies are deep, visible channels. Chambal ravines are the classic result of unchecked gully erosion.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Disease) with List-II (Causative pollutant):
List-I
A. Minamata disease
B. Itai-itai disease
C. Blue baby syndrome
D. Skeletal fluorosis
List-II
1. Mercury
2. Cadmium
3. Nitrate in drinking water
4. Excess fluoride
questions.e: Minamata was caused by methyl mercury in fish in Japan, and itai-itai by cadmium in rice and water. Nitrates cause methaemoglobinaemia in infants, and excess fluoride in groundwater damages teeth and bones.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bhopal gas tragedy of 1984:
1. The gas that leaked was methyl isocyanate.
2. The gas that leaked was phosgene.
3. The disaster was followed by the enactment of the Public Liability Insurance Act in 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The leak at the Union Carbide pesticide plant was of methyl isocyanate (MIC). The tragedy exposed the lack of liability rules, leading to the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 and the Public Liability Insurance Act 1991.

questions.q: Target 15.3 of the Sustainable Development Goals seeks, by 2030, to
o: double the area under protected forests worldwide
combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, and strive for a land degradation neutral world
end all use of chemical fertilisers
questions.e: Land degradation neutrality means any land lost to degradation is offset by restoration elsewhere. It links SDG 15 with the work of the UNCCD.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about REDD+:
1. It includes conservation of forest carbon stocks.
2. It includes sustainable management of forests.
3. It includes enhancement of forest carbon stocks.
4. It is a project mechanism of the Kyoto Protocol's Clean Development Mechanism.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: REDD+ comes from the UNFCCC process, not from the Kyoto CDM. It rewards developing countries on a results-based basis for lower deforestation and degradation, and adds conservation, sustainable management and enhancement of forest carbon stocks.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India State of Forest Report (ISFR):
1. The Forest Survey of India functions under the Ministry of Agriculture.
2. It is published by the Forest Survey of India.
3. It is released every two years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: FSI, headquartered in Dehradun, is a body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It maps forest cover through satellite data and field inventories, and the report is biennial.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about forest classification under the Indian Forest Act, 1927:
1. In reserved forests, activities are prohibited unless specifically permitted.
2. In protected forests, activities are generally permitted unless specifically prohibited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The default rule is reversed between the two. Reserved forests are the most restricted category, and protected forests allow customary rights unless banned.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; Indian Forest Act 1927

questions.q: According to the UNCCD, 'desertification' refers to
o: the natural advance of existing deserts into neighbouring regions
land degradation only in hyper-arid regions
loss of vegetation in cold polar regions
land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas resulting from various factors including climatic variations and human activities
questions.e: Desertification is not just deserts expanding. It is degradation of dryland productivity from both climate and human pressure such as overgrazing or poor irrigation.

questions.q: At the global level, the largest direct driver of tropical deforestation is
questions.e: Clearing for cattle pasture, soybean and oil palm accounts for most tropical forest loss. This is why supply-chain commitments are central in forest policy.

questions.q:
Consider the following possible consequences of large-scale deforestation:
1. Reduced transpiration may lower local and regional rainfall.
2. Greater surface runoff and soil erosion.
3. Higher groundwater recharge.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Without canopy and root systems, rain runs off quickly and carries soil away, so less water infiltrates and recharge falls, not rises. Fewer trees also means less water vapour returned to the air.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Minamata disease in Japan affected people who ate fish from polluted bay waters.
Statement-II: Mercury biomagnifies along the aquatic food chain, reaching high concentrations in top predators.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Industrial effluent released mercury, which was converted into methyl mercury and built up from plankton to fish to people. Biomagnification explains why a very small discharge produced severe nervous system damage.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Byssinosis : Inhalation of cotton fibre dust
Bagassosis : Inhalation of sugarcane bagasse dust
questions.e: Asbestosis is caused by asbestos fibres. Coal dust causes coal workers' pneumoconiosis, or black lung disease.

questions.q: Which one of the following measures is most effective in reducing wind erosion of soil in arid and semi-arid regions?
questions.e: Rows of trees break the wind speed near the ground, so fewer soil particles are lifted. Contour ploughing and terraces mainly check water erosion on slopes.

questions.q: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed on
questions.e: The day marks the adoption of the UNCCD on 17 June 1994. 5 June is World Environment Day, 22 April is Earth Day and 21 March is the International Day of Forests.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of pollutants and conditions best explains eutrophication of lakes?
o: Excess carbon monoxide leading to acidification
Excess chlorine leading to loss of salinity
Excess nitrogen and phosphorus leading to algal blooms and oxygen depletion
questions.e: Runoff of fertilisers and sewage feeds algae. When the algae die, their decomposition uses up the dissolved oxygen and fish die.

questions.q: The Taungya system is a type of
o: agroforestry in which food crops are grown between young forest tree seedlings
questions.e: Farmers prepare the land, raise crops and tend the saplings for the first years until the canopy closes. This is why it is regarded as an early agroforestry method.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about people's movements for forest and environment protection:
1. The Chipko movement began in the Chamoli region of present-day Uttarakhand.
2. The Appiko movement took place in the Western Ghats region of Karnataka.
3. The Silent Valley movement in Kerala opposed a hydroelectric project on the Kunthipuzha river.
4. The Silent Valley movement opposed a project on the Periyar river.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Silent Valley was about the Kunthipuzha, a tributary of the Bharathapuzha, not the Periyar, so statement 4 is wrong. Appiko, in Uttara Kannada, borrowed the idea of hugging trees from Chipko.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Brundtland Commission:
1. It was set up after the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.
2. It was formally the World Commission on Environment and Development.
3. Its report 'Our Common Future' was published in 1987.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Commission, chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, reported in 1987 and defined sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Its report in fact prepared the ground for Rio in 1992.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Stockholm Conference of 1972:
1. It was the first major UN conference on the human environment.
2. Its Declaration contained 26 principles.
3. It led to the establishment of the United Nations Environment Programme.
4. It adopted Agenda 21.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Agenda 21 was adopted at Rio in 1992. Stockholm gave the Declaration with 26 principles, and UNEP was created by the UN General Assembly later in 1972 in response.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Rio Declaration principle) with List-II (idea):
List-I
A. Principle 7
B. Principle 10
C. Principle 15
D. Principle 16
List-II
1. Precautionary approach
2. Polluter pays
3. Common but differentiated responsibilities
4. Public participation in environmental issues
questions.e: These are the best known principles of the 1992 Rio Declaration: CBDR (7), participation (10), precaution (15) and polluter pays (16).

questions.q:
Consider the following events:
1. Publication of the Brundtland Report
2. Stockholm Conference
3. Rio+20 Conference
4. World Summit on Sustainable Development at Johannesburg
Arrange them in chronological order.
questions.e: Stockholm was in 1972, the Brundtland Report in 1987, Johannesburg in 2002 and Rio+20 in 2012. Each conference reviewed the promise of the previous one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
1. There are 17 goals and 169 targets.
2. They were adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda.
3. They are legally binding on all member states.
4. They succeeded the Millennium Development Goals.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The SDGs are voluntary and country-led, so statement 3 is wrong. They succeeded the MDGs, whose term ended in 2015.

questions.q:
Match List-I (SDG) with List-II (Goal number):
List-I
A. Clean Water and Sanitation
B. Responsible Consumption and Production
C. Life Below Water
D. Life on Land
List-II
1. SDG 12
2. SDG 14
3. SDG 15
4. SDG 6
questions.e: SDG 6 is water and sanitation, 12 is responsible consumption and production, 14 life below water (oceans) and 15 life on land.
questions.h: Land comes after water: 14 water, 15 land.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the SDGs in India:
1. NITI Aayog is the nodal institution for coordinating the SDGs in India.
2. The SDG India Index is prepared by the Ministry of Statistics.
3. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has developed a National Indicator Framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NITI Aayog both coordinates the SDGs and brings out the SDG India Index. MoSPI's role is the indicator framework for monitoring progress.

questions.q:
With reference to the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006, consider the following statements:
1. It was issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. Category A projects are appraised at the Central level by an Expert Appraisal Committee.
3. Category A projects are appraised by the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Category A projects, which are larger or more sensitive, are handled by the Centre. Category B projects go to the State Expert Appraisal Committee and SEIAA, so statement 3 mixes up the two.

questions.q: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the correct sequence of stages is
questions.e: Screening decides whether a project needs EIA (for Category B). Scoping then fixes the terms of reference, public consultation hears affected people on the draft report, and appraisal precedes the clearance decision.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about EIA:
1. The United States was the first country to legislate EIA, through its National Environmental Policy Act of 1969.
2. EIA was first made statutory in India through the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. In India, EIA began with the assessment of river valley projects in 1976-77.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: EIA became statutory in India through a 1994 notification under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986, later replaced by the 2006 notification. The Wildlife Act has no such role.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Both were inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
2. Article 48A, a Directive Principle, directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
3. Article 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both provisions were inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, passed shortly after the Stockholm Conference. The 44th Amendment dealt mainly with undoing some Emergency-era changes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 42nd Amendment moved 'forests' from the State List to the Concurrent List.
2. Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate on a State subject to implement an international agreement.
3. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted by Parliament in pursuance of the Stockholm decisions under Article 253.
4. Environment protection is expressly listed as a separate entry in the Concurrent List.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Seventh Schedule has no standalone entry on environment, so Parliament relied on Article 253 for the EPA. Forests, and protection of wild animals and birds, were moved to the Concurrent List in 1976.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Principle or doctrine) with List-II (Case):
List-I
A. Public trust doctrine
B. Absolute liability
C. Precautionary principle
D. Polluter pays principle
List-II
1. Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
2. M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath
3. M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas leak)
4. Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
questions.e: Kamal Nath concerned a motel on the Beas river, the Oleum gas case produced absolute liability, Vellore (tannery pollution) applied precaution and the Bichhri case (Enviro-Legal Action) applied polluter pays.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court has held that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to a healthy environment.
Statement-II: Article 21 expressly mentions the word 'environment'.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The right to clean air and water has been read into Article 21 through judicial interpretation, as in Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar. The text of Article 21 itself speaks only of life and personal liberty.

questions.q:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
2. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
3. Wildlife (Protection) Act
4. Environment (Protection) Act
Arrange them in the chronological order of enactment.
questions.e: The Wildlife Act came in 1972, the Water Act in 1974, the Air Act in 1981 and the umbrella EPA in 1986, after Bhopal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Conservation Act, 1980:
1. It requires prior approval of the Central Government for diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes.
2. It was amended in 2023 and renamed the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam.
3. It applies only to forests within Protected Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act was passed to stop rapid diversion of forest land by States and applies to forests generally, not only Protected Areas. The 2023 amendment renamed it.

questions.q: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 provides for
o: compensation only after proof of negligence by the owner
punishment for trade in endangered species
immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances, on a no-fault basis
questions.e: After Bhopal, the Act made owners of hazardous units take insurance so that victims need not wait for a court to establish fault. It also created an Environmental Relief Fund.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Biological Diversity Act, 2002:
1. The National Biodiversity Authority functions under the Ministry of Agriculture.
2. It was enacted to give effect to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
3. The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered in Chennai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NBA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It works with State Biodiversity Boards and local Biodiversity Management Committees.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Agenda 21:
1. It is a non-binding action plan adopted at the Rio Earth Summit of 1992.
2. It is a legally binding treaty.
3. It encourages local authorities to prepare local plans for sustainable development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Agenda 21 is a voluntary programme for the twenty-first century. Its Local Agenda 21 idea asks municipalities to translate global goals into local action.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rio+20 Conference of 2012:
1. Its outcome document was titled 'The Future We Want'.
2. It adopted the Millennium Development Goals.
3. It replaced the Commission on Sustainable Development with a High-Level Political Forum.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The MDGs date from 2000. Rio+20 started the process that led to the SDGs and set up the High-Level Political Forum in place of the CSD.

questions.q: In Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996), the Supreme Court held which of the following to be essential features of sustainable development?
o: Public trust doctrine and absolute liability
Precautionary principle and polluter pays principle
Right to development and sovereign immunity
questions.e: The Court recognised that sustainable development, with the precautionary principle and polluter pays, forms part of the law of the land. The case arose from tannery pollution in Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Under the public trust doctrine, as applied by the Supreme Court in Indian environmental cases, the State
o: has absolute ownership of natural resources and may dispose of them as it pleases
holds natural resources such as air, water and forests as trustee for the public and cannot freely transfer them for private use
must lease all forests to local communities
is liable for damage to the environment regardless of fault
questions.e: The doctrine comes from Roman law and was adopted in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath. The last option describes absolute liability, a different doctrine.

questions.q:
Statement-I: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June every year.
Statement-II: The Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment opened on 5 June 1972.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The UN General Assembly chose the opening date of the Stockholm Conference as the date for the annual day, and the first one was observed in 1974. This is why Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q: The Ecological Footprint is a measure of
o: the carbon stored in forests in tonnes
the species diversity of a biome
human demand on the biosphere's regenerative capacity, expressed in global hectares
the population density per square kilometre of habitat
questions.e: Comparing footprint with biocapacity shows whether a population lives within its ecological means. Overshoot means consuming resources faster than nature can regenerate them.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs):
1. They comprised eight goals to be achieved by 2015.
2. Goal 7 related to ensuring environmental sustainability.
3. They were adopted at the Rio+20 Conference in 2012.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The MDGs came from the Millennium Declaration of 2000. Rio+20 in 2012 began the process for the post-2015 SDGs.
